attacks.claim: S2's golden-table instruction is inexecutable and hides the one payload shape that actually ships: 'output:<a real OutputConfig.id from DEFAULT_KIT>' cannot be built because DEFAULT_KIT.outputs is the empty array. Real output ids are minted by core's reconcileOutputs as the strings `output:1`, `output:2`, ... — so live flow-node ids are the DOUBLE-PREFIXED `output:output:<n>`. The plan's decoder spec states verbatim defensive rules only for drum-id rejoin and hoop last-segment; it never states the output rule (payload = everything after the FIRST colon, startsWith-based like today's parseOutputNodeId at patch-graph.ts:70-72). An implementer writing the grammar as `<kind>:<a>[:<b>]` with a split(':') decode returns outputId 'output' for `output:output:3`, and routingFromGraph then keys the routing on a wrong id for every reconciled port — the common case, not the adversarial one.
attacks.evidence: packages/core/src/model/defaults.ts:46 `outputs: []` (DEFAULT_KIT has no outputs); packages/core/src/geometry/kit-schema.ts:508-531 reconcileOutputs mints OutputConfig ids `output:<n>`; apps/web/src/lib/app/patch-graph.ts:64-72 outputNodeId/parseOutputNodeId are prefix-concat/startsWith, so outputNodeId('output:1') === 'output:output:1'. S2's table lists 'output:' and 'garbage' as adversarial cases but never the double-prefix id.
attacks.repair: In S2: state the output decode rule explicitly ('output' kind claims everything after the first colon; never split), replace the DEFAULT_KIT sourcing with ids from reconcileOutputs (e.g. `output:output:1`), and add `output:output:3` to the golden table with baseline parseOutputNodeId output pasted as the expected literal.

attacks.repair: Drop zoneNodeId from S2's exports (keep only the decoder's zone ARM, which needs no encoder), or explicitly amend the knip acceptance line to exempt zoneNodeId pending Trent's answer to open_questions #2.

attacks.claim: S6's proposed 'correction' to the kit-schema.ts:508 comment is itself false. That comment describes OutputConfig.id VALUES — reconcileOutputs literally mints config ids of the form `output:<n>` (kit-schema.ts:530 `const id = \`output:${n}\``). Rewriting it to say 'port ids are `output:<OutputConfig.id>`' conflates the config id with the FLOW-NODE id (which is `output:` + config id, i.e. `output:output:<n>`), replacing a slightly-stale comment with a wrong one in core.
attacks.evidence: packages/core/src/geometry/kit-schema.ts:508 ('Appended port ids are `output:<n>`') and :529-531 (the minting loop) — the ids being documented ARE OutputConfig.id values, not patch-graph node ids. S6 intent (plan line 85) says 'correct the kit-schema.ts note to say port ids are `output:<OutputConfig.id>`'.
attacks.repair: S6's kit-schema edit should say: appended OutputConfig ids are the strings `output:<n>` (a naming legacy of the old positional grammar), and the patch graph's flow-node id for any output is `output:<OutputConfig.id>` — i.e. `output:output:<n>` for appended ports — decoded by patch-node-id.ts.

attacks.claim: S5's `moveZoneSlot(map, from: ZoneRef, to: ZoneRef)` silently widens the function's domain: today's signature (map, drumId, oldSlot, newSlot) makes a cross-drum move inexpressible, and the body is documented as 'a re-label'. With two full ZoneRefs, from.drumId !== to.drumId becomes representable and the plan never says what it means — the naive composition (removeZone(from) + add/set(to)) would MOVE a zone between drums, a behaviour change no test pins and DrumZonesList.svelte (the only caller, line 69) never exercises. An implementer cannot execute the step unambiguously.
attacks.evidence: apps/web/src/lib/app/docks/patch-inspector.ts:283-293 (moveZoneSlot body and 're-label' doc comment); apps/web/src/lib/app/docks/inspectors/DrumZonesList.svelte:69 sole call site passes one drumId. Plan S5 intent (line 70) specifies the new signature but no drumId-mismatch rule.
attacks.repair: One sentence in S5: when from.drumId !== to.drumId, either return map unchanged (preserve today's re-label-only semantics) — recommended — and add a test pinning it; cross-drum moves stay out of scope.

attacks.claim: S5's rebasing of the three map schemas onto zoneRefSchema can silently reshuffle persisted-project JSON key order or shift the slot default, and the vitest suite has no snapshot pinning either — a green suite would not catch a changed on-disk shape.

attacks.plan_response: S5's verification and behaviour_parity_evidence_plan check 5 buy a dedicated byte-parity script precisely because the suite cannot prove this: baseline-vs-post parse of a real project plus pathological maps (missing slot, 0, 7, out-of-range 9, unknown keys), asserting deepStrictEqual AND JSON.stringify byte-equality AND the identical throw path; known_gaps names the missing key-order snapshot explicitly. triggerBindingSchema's required-vs-defaulted slot trap is also pre-answered — S5 deliberately leaves it literal, echoing the phase-3 refuter.
